channel.title: Merkle Street
channel.description: Merkle Street reports crypto news on Bitcoin, Ethereum, layer 2s, DeFi, stablecoins, exchanges, regulation, security incidents and protocol upgrades.

item.title: Choose the XMR-to-EVM Route Before You Send
item.description: Choose an XMR-to-EVM route by the asset you need and trust you accept: atomic swaps, intermediaries and wrapped claims distribute risk and recovery differently.

item.title: What One-to-One XMR Redemption Actually Returns
item.description: A one-to-one XMR redemption returns the wrapped token’s backing amount, while fees, confirmation waits and Sepolia’s test status shape what arrives and what it means.

item.title: A Cross-Chain Swap Simulation Must Test the Destination
item.description: A cross-chain swap simulation checks each leg before funds move, exposing destination gas, slippage and contract failures a source-chain quote can miss.

item.title: Why Polygon deposits get rejected: check the network first
item.description: A Polygon deposit can confirm on-chain and still miss an account credit: check the selected network, token contract, destination, confirmations and minimum first.

item.title: Plan Polygon Bridge Withdrawals Around the Payout
item.description: Plan Polygon PoS withdrawals by burning tokens on Polygon, waiting for an Ethereum checkpoint, then claiming on Ethereum; allow time and gas for both transactions.

item.title: What to Do When an Omnichain Destination Pauses
item.description: A paused destination does not always mean lost funds: trace the message, check the route status, and resume or recover only through the bridge’s process.

item.title: When a Destination Chain Goes Down, Bound the Queue
item.description: When a destination chain stalls, a bounded, ordered message queue limits congestion while preserving retries, clear status and safe recovery for cross-chain users.

item.title: Omnichain State Starts With the Consistency You Need
item.description: Choose omnichain state by deciding which updates must agree across chains, how long they can wait, and how the application handles stale or conflicting data.

item.title: Why a Treasury Route Goes Missing and How to Trace It
item.description: A missing treasury route usually means no usable quote passed the router’s checks; trace the source balance, token support, liquidity and destination conditions in order.

item.title: How to Compare Cross-Chain Swap Routes by Total Cost
item.description: A cross-chain route is cheapest only after bridge fees, swap pricing, gas, slippage and the destination amount are compared on the same basis before signing.

item.title: Why the Same Token Has Different Versions on Different Chains
item.description: A token can appear on several chains because each network has its own contract, while bridges create representations that may track the same asset without sharing its code.

item.title: How Thin Liquidity Distorts a BSC Token’s Market Cap
item.description: A thin BSC token pool can imply a large market cap because a small trade sets the quoted price, even when holders cannot sell much near that level.

item.title: Check a BSC Token Contract Before You Swap
item.description: A BSC token swap calls a contract through a pool, so check the address, verified code, owner permissions, liquidity and token approval before signing a transaction.

item.title: How to Track Cost Basis Across a Crypto Bridge
item.description: A bridge moves assets across ledgers, but the record must connect both sides; that link lets you preserve cost basis and separate transfers from disposals.

item.title: Moving Mantle sale proceeds to Ethereum for a tax reserve
item.description: A Mantle sale can create a tax liability before the cash reaches Ethereum; bridge the proceeds, keep fee and transaction records, and reserve the amount your local rules require.

item.title: Mantle Bridge Moves App Funds Between Ethereum and Mantle
item.description: Mantle Bridge moves ETH, MNT and tokens between Ethereum and Mantle; learn how deposits and withdrawals work, and what to check before using an app.

item.title: Bridge the Amount a Manta Payment Needs
item.description: Bridge only the asset and amount the payment needs, reserve native gas on both networks, and check the asset, network and return route before signing.

item.title: How to Check a Bridge Contract in a Network Explorer
item.description: Check a bridge contract in a network explorer to match its address, code and transaction history to the right network before authorizing a transfer.

item.title: What a Bridge Upgrade Notice Means for Long-Term Holdings
item.description: A bridge upgrade notice can change where a transfer is sent or how it is verified; long-term holders should check the route, deadline and withdrawal path.

item.title: How Much Crypto Should You Send From Your Wallet?
item.description: Send the recipient’s exact amount, then check that your wallet can also pay the network fee and preserve any balance you need for later transactions.
